correctness.rationale: Gauss survivor E(1/N) has continued-fraction digits all >=N (up to countably many endpoints); inverse branches 1/(a+x) on [0,1/N] satisfy (a+1/N)^-2<=|phi_a prime|<=a^-2 and open-set/bounded-distortion countable IFS hypotheses. Pressure zero lies between Hurwitz sums V_N(s)=zeta(2s,N+1/N) and U_N(s)=zeta(2s,N). At U_N(s+)=1, 1-V_N(s+)<=2/N^2; on [s-,s+] have -V_N prime>=log N; root width<=2/(N^2 log N). Euler–Maclaurin U_N(1/2+e)=N^-2e/(2e)+N^-1-2e/2+O(N^-2-2e). The integral root e0=W(log N)/(2log N) and Taylor derivative 2log N+1/e0 give the displayed lattice correction e0/[N(2log N+1/e0)]=W(log N)^2/(4N(log N)^2(1+W(log N))) with O(1/(N^2 log N) remainder. Adjacent inverse-integer hole parameters squeeze arbitrary alpha leading law. Independent 55-digit bisections at N=10,100,1000 checked distinct Hurwitz roots, enclosure and leading correction; these are bounded diagnostics only. The countable IFS theorem is a standard cited premise.

value.rationale: It quantifies the natural zero-hole Gauss survivor dimension jump with a Lambert-W boundary layer and a genuinely resolvable discrete alphabet correction. The two zeta roots furnish a computationally tractable uniform numerical certificate for every N>=2. This is substantially finer than the known 1/2 limit and general pressure method; no broader theorem is demanded.

limitations: Pressure bracket is not an exact dimension formula; holes all alpha only leading order; numerical checks finite; malformed source prose requires publication correction.
residual_risks: An older Good-type restricted continued-fraction dimension expansion may cover part or all of novelty.
